# llvm-dsdl identifier role policy (golden)
#
# Generated by test/unit/NamingGoldenTests.cpp. Do not edit by hand.
# Regenerate:  LLVMDSDL_UPDATE_NAMING_GOLDEN=1 <build>/test/unit/llvmdsdl-unit-tests
#
# The table below is what the six emitters do, not an aspiration: every cell was taken
# from the call site that produces that name, and NamingPolicyTests.cpp asserts each one
# against the projection that call site uses.
#
# escape  replaces characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_] and prefixes a leading digit.
# strop   escapes a result that collides with a language keyword.
# upper   upper-cases the finished identifier.
#
# The 'no' cells are deliberate, not unfinished. A C or C++ header stem is a file name
# rather than an identifier, and a C or C++ macro token is not in the language's
# namespace and always carries its type name as a prefix, so neither needs a keyword
# escape. Names the generated code has already claimed are a separate question and are
# still checked -- see the claimed-name cases in NamingPolicyTests.cpp.

== role policy ==

language role           case      escape  strop  upper
------------------------------------------------------
c        TypeName       preserve  yes     yes    no
c        FieldName      preserve  yes     yes    no
c        ConstantName   preserve  yes     no     yes
c        FunctionName   preserve  yes     yes    no

c        NamespaceName  preserve  yes     yes    no
c        FileStem       preserve  no      no     no
c        MacroName      preserve  yes     no     yes

== scopes ==
#
# NamingScope over one region of generated code, in declaration order. Where a role's
# projection is many-to-one the scope appends _2, _3, ... so the map stays injective; the
# reserved scenario shows a field escaping a name the generated methods already own.
# C, C++ and Rust keep the DSDL spelling for fields, so they need no repair at all -- the
# same scope is only lossy in the backends that fold case.

scope                 language source        identifier
-----------------------------------------------------------------
struct_body           c        fooBar        fooBar
struct_body           c        foo_bar       foo_bar
struct_body           c        FooBar        FooBar
struct_body           c        break         break_
struct_body           c        break_        break__2
struct_body           cpp      fooBar        fooBar
struct_body           cpp      foo_bar       foo_bar
struct_body           cpp      FooBar        FooBar
struct_body           cpp      break         break_
struct_body           cpp      break_        break__2
struct_body           rust     fooBar        fooBar
struct_body           rust     foo_bar       foo_bar
struct_body           rust     FooBar        FooBar
struct_body           rust     break         break_
struct_body           rust     break_        break__2
struct_body           go       fooBar        FooBar
struct_body           go       foo_bar       FooBar_2
struct_body           go       FooBar        FooBar_3
struct_body           go       break         Break
struct_body           go       break_        Break_2
struct_body           ts       fooBar        foo_bar
struct_body           ts       foo_bar       foo_bar_2
struct_body           ts       FooBar        foo_bar_3
struct_body           ts       break         break_
struct_body           ts       break_        break__2
struct_body           python   fooBar        foo_bar
struct_body           python   foo_bar       foo_bar_2
struct_body           python   FooBar        foo_bar_3
struct_body           python   break         break_
struct_body           python   break_        break__2
